name: What does the cabin interior sealing process involve?

mainEntity.name: What does the cabin interior sealing process involve?

acceptedAnswer.text: The process begins with cleaning log surfaces and removing failed, loose sealant or debris from seams. If gaps are deep, backing material like backer rod is inserted so the sealant bonds only to the top and bottom log edges, allowing proper flex. The crew then applies an elastomeric chinking or compatible interior sealant, tooling the joint smooth with specialized trowels or brushes. Finally, log faces receive any required touch-up finish or clear protective coat. Working with a finish contractor like HH Remodeling ensures that trim transitions, drywall junctions, and carpentry work align neatly with the sealed logs.
acceptedAnswer.description: The process includes clearing out old sealant, inserting backer rod in deep joints, applying and tooling flexible sealant, and finishing with protective topcoats.
